Commentary.Commentary: The players are back out in the middle. A new opening pair for Bangladesh strides out in Tanzid Hasan and Parvez Hossain Emon. India's latest sensation, pacer Mayank Yadav, will have the white cherry in his hand. Emon to pace.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

What are we looking at in this game, realistically? Already, the highest wins by India in T20Is and lowest totals by Bangladesh in this format would be checked. 273 is the biggest margin of victory in all T20Is by Nepal, while for India, it is 168 runs against New Zealand in Ahmedabad in 2023. The second case could have a better likelihood tonight. As far as Bangladesh, surely they would aim to bat better than 70 all out against New Zealand at the Eden Gardens in 2016. But above all, can we have a good game of cricket? This is all too one-sided.

Dussehra is being celebrated in the whole of India today, but it is Diwali which has come early for the home side. The term 'fearless cricket' was defined comprehensively as the batters simply batted to their potential and enjoyed their game. Whether Bangladesh bowled well or not, is another issue. But to keep backing yourself to clear the ropes and find the boundaries at will and that too, not one, but nearly the whole batting unit, means a lot of kudos needs to be given to the coach and the captain for instilling the belief. Samson started the saga, SKY just was himself but barring Abhishek Sharma, everyone enjoyed himself in the top 5.

A difficult day for Najmul Hossain Shanto as he just kept looking at the heavens time and again, probably secretly hoping that the rain forecast comes true at some stage. He was helpless as the ball and the bowlers were cantered to all parts. Tanzim Hasan Sakib picked up 3 wickets but it was more because he got a couple at the end. Everyone else was hammered, with Mahedi Hasan's 4-0-45-0 actually being the pick of the evening!

The game started decently for the visitors with Tanzim Hasan Sakib dismissing Abhishek Sharma early. But after that, they were simply up against it. Sanju Samson and Suryakumar Yadav just tore into the bowling and registered a mammoth 173-run stand in just 69 balls for the second wicket with Samson registering his maiden T20I ton. The tourists did manage to get rid of SKY soon but they just could not stop the bleeding of runs as the middle order came to the party.

Let's observe a minute's silence as a mourning for all the Bangladesh bowlers. They have conceded 297 runs, the highest score by a Test-playing nation and second highest overall. 22 sixes and 25 fours - that's 232 runs in 47 balls alone - meaning in the remaining 73, Bangladesh conceded 65. It is a flat deck, but the bowlers were totally flat in this game.

SIX! BANG! Rinku Singh finishes the innings in some style! India end just three runs short of 300! Tanzim Hasan Sakib looks to attack the stumps, on a fuller length, Rinku Singh clears his front leg and smashes it out of sight over deep mid-wicket for a biggie.

Commentary.Commentary: Meanwhile, shifting focus slightly to the Eves, Bangladesh ain't doing better there either. Choosing to bat first in an important T20 World Cup match against South Africa, Bangladesh are 8/1 after 4 overs, going nowhere. In Hyderabad, they are travelling everywhere while in Dubai, they have been stalled. Aha. Electricity has been restored. Back to India.

Oh dear. One of the light towers has suddenly become dysfunctional. All the light bulbs have gone off and we are forced into a stoppage. In a way, it might be better for Bangladesh, as it gives them some time to stop and think. If they continue to just go through the motions, this Indian batting lineup might well target 300 tonight. The pitch seems to be as flat as a pancake and the Indians are just baking the bowlers and then frying them out. Everyone has been given a tour of Hyderabad with the exception of Mahedi Hasan, who has just about managed to stave off some respect.
Fuller, outside off, Yadav gets down and sweeps it behind square leg for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 8.3: Mahedi Hasan to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! STUPENDOUS! Tossed up, outside off, Suryakumar Yadav gets down on a knee and mows the slog sweep, to the longer part of the ground. That's why perhaps, the ball didn't go all the way, just bounced in front of the ropes.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 8.2: Mahedi Hasan to Suryakumar Yadav, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Mahedi Hasan is back on now. Starts with a short ball, outside off, gets it to move away off the deck, probably a carrom ball. Sanju Samson rocks back and slaps a pull down to long off for a single. Moves to 60 (27).
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 8.1: Mahedi Hasan to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: BYE! A slower bumper, on middle. Sanju Samson leans back and tries to ramp it away but fails to gets any bat on it. The wicket-keeper fumbles which allows the batter to collect a bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.6: Mustafizur Rahman to Sanju Samson, Bye.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! The umpire now extends his arms. It is fuller, down the leg side. Samson looks to clip it away but misses. Wide called.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.6: Mustafizur Rahman to Sanju Samson, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Incredible hit. Sanju Samson goes inside out this time and sends it sailing over the ropes. Whatever he is touching is turning into gold here. Good length, angling across, outside off. Sanju Samson stays on his back foot and smokes it over extra covers. It goes all the way.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.5: Mustafizur Rahman to Sanju Samson, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: A length ball, wide of off. Yadav slaps it through point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.4: Mustafizur Rahman to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Another slower ball, on the shorter side, Sanju Samson pulls it down to long on for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.3: Mustafizur Rahman to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Better length, nearly a yorker, outside off, Yadav dabs it towards cover for a single. The stand moves to 80 from 31 balls.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.2: Mustafizur Rahman to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! A bit too predictable. Suryakumar Yadav knows that the slower one is coming and is ready. Gets it right in the slot, outside off, waits for it to arrive and carves it over cover. Moves to 40 (16). 100 UP FOR INDIA IN 7.1 OVERS!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.1: Mustafizur Rahman to Suryakumar Yadav, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Rishad Hossain will be happy with the way he ended his over, a good comeback from him. Although, the scorecard is a scary looking one for Bangladesh. Length, around middle and leg. Suryakumar Yadav goes back and pushes it towards mid on. They take a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.6: Rishad Hossain to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: It is short once again, width on offer for Suryakumar Yadav. He waits for it and goes for the cut, but does not time it at all. He only manages to find the fielder at backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.5: Rishad Hossain to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shorter, around off, turning away off the deck. Sanju Samson waits for it and dabs it towards point. They cross for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.4: Rishad Hossain to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Just over! 22-BALL FIFTY FOR SAMSON, THE FASTEST BY AN INDIAN AGAINST BANGLADESH IN T20IS! A sparkling knock for sure. Fuller, outside off, Sanju Samson leans in this time. Gets into the shot, reaches the pitch and lofts it inside out over cover. Long off is pretty wide, to his left and for a second, it seems like it is going straight to him. But it is just above his leap. The stand is worth 73 (26).
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.3: Rishad Hossain to Sanju Samson, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR MORE! Bangladesh are already looking down and out. Another half tracker, around off, Samson goes back and pulls it over mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Rishad Hossain to Sanju Samson, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Will Rishad be able to stem the run flow?

FOUR! Welcome into the attack. Short, outside off, Sanju Samson stays back, picks the length in a trice and goes inside out, on the back foot, over cover. Moves to 41 (20) and the stand is worth 63 (24).
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Rishad Hossain to Sanju Samson, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! WHAT A HIT! Suryakumar Yadav moves to 35 now. Tanzim Hasan Sakib with a half-tracker, on off. Suryakumar Yadav gets a hold of it and bludgeons it over the mid-wicket fence. It goes straight into the stands.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Suryakumar Yadav, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Make it three on the trot. Suryakumar Yadav making sure that he makes the most of the Powerplay. It is full, on the pads. Suryakumar Yadav reads it quickly and flicks it into mid-wicket. It goes along the ground and races away to the boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Suryakumar Yadav, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Consecutive boundaries for SKY! Tanzim Hasan Sakib with a good-length ball, around middle, nips in a bit. Suryakumar Yadav stands tall, gets under it and smacks it over mid-wicket. The ball takes a bounce and heads into the ropes.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Suryakumar Yadav, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Up and over! On a length, around off, Suryakumar Yadav comes forward and lofts it on the up, over mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Suryakumar Yadav, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Oohhh.. goes for the inswinging yorker, but ends up bowling a full toss, down the leg side. Sanju Samson looks to flick but plays it early and gets a leading edge towards mid off. The batters take a quick single and there is a direct hit at the striker's end, but Suryakumar Yadav is well in. The ball deflects wide of the backup fielder at square leg but SKY declines the overthrow.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slower ball, on a good length, outside off, Sanju Samson pushes it towards cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! This is even better. Suryakumar Yadav making sure the momentum remains with them. It is short, on the bodyline. Suryakumar Yadav swivels and smokes it over the deep square leg fence for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Taskin Ahmed to Suryakumar Yadav, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Full ball, on the pads. Samson tucks it into the leg side for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Taskin Ahmed to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! What a shot. Short ball, angled into the body. Sanju Samson exposes all his stumps and pulls it powerfully over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Taskin Ahmed to Sanju Samson, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: A length ball, sliding down leg. Yadav leaves it alone. The ball brushes the pads and rolls out. The batters are quick to pick up a leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Taskin Ahmed to Suryakumar Yadav, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR LEG BYES! The runs continue to flow for India. Taskin Ahmed serves a full ball into the pads. Suryakumar Yadav tries to flick it away but misses. The ball brushes the pads and runs down to the fine leg fence for a boundary. 50 UP FOR INDIA IN 4.2 OVERS!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Taskin Ahmed to Suryakumar Yadav, 4 Leg byes.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, outside off. Yadav dabs it towards short third but for no run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Taskin Ahmed to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slower and shorter, on leg. This one bounces a bit extra than what Suryakumar Yadav expected. He fends it out off the top half of his blade. The ball trickles into the leg side. The batters cross for a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Mustafizur Rahman to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full ball, on the pads. Samson stays back and flicks it behind square on the leg side for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Mustafizur Rahman to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! BANG! This is outstanding batting. Sanju Samson couldn't have hit it any better. Mustafizur Rahman once again rolls his fingers over the ball and pitches it up, on off. Samson steps out of the crease, gets under it and smokes it down the park for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Mustafizur Rahman to Sanju Samson, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Sanju Samson gets a hold of this one. It is very full, outside off. Mustafizur Rahman follows the batter outside leg. Sanju Samson creates some room and whips it over mid-wicket for a cracking boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Mustafizur Rahman to Sanju Samson, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: A bit short, but hardly any pace on offer. Sanju Samson mistimes his pull towards mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Mustafizur Rahman to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Mustafizur Rahman starts with a slower one, on a good-length, angling across, outside off. Sanju Samson looks to punch it away off his back foot, but gets no bat on it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Mustafizur Rahman to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fourth bowler in as many overs! Mustafizur Rahman is introduced into the attack now.

FOUR! One bounce and into the ropes. Tanzim Hasan Sakib started this over with a wicket, but could not really control the run flow. This is full, tailing into the pads. Suryakumar Yadav picks up nicely and flicks it towards deep mid-wicket. The fielder in the deep rushes to his left but could not get there in time.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Suryakumar Yadav, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: A slight halt in play as one of the bails seems to have stopped working. The fourth umpire sprints in with a replacement bail. We are now good to resume!
Full ball, around off. Yadav comes forward and eases it to mid on but finds the fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! This one flies over the keeper's head. It is a sharp bumper, on middle. Suryakumar Yadav picks up early, goes for the hook. The ball catches the outside edge and flies down to deep third for a huge six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Suryakumar Yadav, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller, on middle. Sanju Samson gets it to square leg off the inside edge. They take a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Waste of a review here. It is very full, angled into the pads. Suryakumar Yadav tries to flick it away but misses. He gets pinged on the boots of his back leg. Tanzim Hasan Sakib appeals but the umpire shows no interest. The ball goes to square leg off the pads. The batters cross for a leg bye in the process. The Ball Tracking confirms that the ball is pitching outside the leg stump line.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Suryakumar Yadav, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Is that out? Tanzim Hasan Sakib has convinced the skipper for a referral on the LBW appeal given Not out by the onfield umpire. It looked to be going down leg to the naked eye, and the replay confirms just that! Bangladesh burn a review!
The Indian skipper, Suryakumar Yadav makes his way out to the middle at number 3!

OUT! CAUGHT! Tanzim Hasan Sakib comes into the attack and strikes instantly. A much-needed breakthrough for Bangladesh. They needed to kill the momentum for India, after Samson struck four boundaries on the trot, and the visitors couldn't have asked for any better than a wicket. It is a short ball, around middle and leg. This one climbs on the batter. Abhishek Sharma is cramped for room as well, but he still goes for the wild heave across the line. The ball catches the top half and balloons to the right of covers. Mahedi Hasan moves to his right, and takes a sharp catch diving forward.
Commentary.Howout: c Mahedi Hasan b Tanzim Hasan Sakib
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Abhishek Sharma, OUT! c Mahedi Hasan b Tanzim Hasan Sakib.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! This is sublime from Sanju Samson and India are not just up and running, they are stomping. Taskin Ahmed serves this into the pads, on a length, asking to be hit. Sanju Samson obliges and flicks it square of the wicket on the leg side for another boundary. 16 from Taskin's opener!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Taskin Ahmed to Sanju Samson, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Easy picking! Taskin Ahmed overcompensates and angles it into the pads, on a length, Sanju Samson flicks it through mid-wicket for the third consecutive boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Taskin Ahmed to Sanju Samson, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Make that two in a row! This is even better than the previous one! Taskin Ahmed pulls the length down a bit and attacks the stumps, Sanju Samson yet again, makes room and with deft hands, times the punch through covers for another boundary.  16 from Taskin's opener!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Taskin Ahmed to Sanju Samson, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Beautiful shot! Too full and at the stumps, Sanju Samson backs away and carves it perfectly through the gap at covers for boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Taskin Ahmed to Sanju Samson, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Continues to keep it tight, on middle and off, on a length, Sanju Samson opens the bat face and steers it to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Taskin Ahmed to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Steams from over the wicket and hurls it right on the money! On a hard length and at the stumps! Sanju Samson gets his bat ahead and taps it to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Taskin Ahmed to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pace from the other end. Taskin Ahmed comes into the attack to share the new ball.

Fires it in, with the angle, on leg, Abhishek Sharma sets himself for a big swipe across the line but misses onto his thigh. A stifled appeal from the bowler alone. Good start from India! 7 runs come off the first over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Mahedi Hasan to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! No sighters needed! Tossed up on off, Abhishek Sharma skips down the track and lofts it over covers for the first boundary of the game.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Mahedi Hasan to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Full and on off, Abhishek Sharma firms his drive straight to the fielder at cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Mahedi Hasan to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller this time, on off, Sanju Samson drives it neatly to deep cover for a single. A huge roar across the stadium as Abhishek Sharma gets on strike.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Mahedi Hasan to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short again, over middle, Sanju Samson is quick to shuffle his weight back and pulls it to the right of deep mid-wicket for a couple of runs. Sanju Samson and India up and running!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Mahedi Hasan to Sanju Samson, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts from over the wicket and lands it a tad shorter in length, on middle and leg, Sanju Samson hops back and tucks it off his pads to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Mahedi Hasan to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: The match is set to begin. The Bangladesh players stride out and take the field. Followed by Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson who walk out to open for India. It is going to be Mahedi Hasan who gets the new ball in hand. Here we go...

Najmul Hossain Shanto is up for a chat. He reveals that they have made two changes, with Mehidy Hasan and Jaker Ali missing out. He emphasizes the importance of the batting group taking responsibility and mentions that they have a solid plan for this game, hoping to execute it flawlessly.

Suryakumar Yadav, the skipper of India says it looks like a good wicket and in the last game as well they wanted to bat first and challenge themselves. Adds that the talk in the group is to continue doing well which will help them just get better and not be complacent. Talks about giving the freedom to the players to go out and express themselves. Concludes that they have one change with Arshdeep missing out and Ravi Bishnoi coming in.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Parvez Hossain Emon, Litton Das (WK), Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Towhid Hridoy, Mahmudullah, Tanzid Hasan (In for Jaker Ali), Rishad Hossain, Taskin Ahmed, Mahedi Hasan (In for Mehidy Hasan), Mustafizur Rahman and Tanzim Hasan Sakib.

India (Playing XI) - Sanju Samson (WK), Abhishek Sharma, Suryakumar Yadav (C), Nitish Kumar Reddy, Hardik Pandya, Riyan Parag, Rinku Singh, Washington Sundar, Varun Chakaravarthy, Ravi Bishnoi (In for Arshdeep Singh) and Mayank Yadav.
TOSS - The coin goes up and lands in favour of India. Suryakumar Yadav informs that they will BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Abhinav Mukund was at the centre earlier for the pitch analysis. He starts by saying that this historically has been a high-scoring venue with the square boundaries being 63 meters and 68 meters while straight is 77 meters which will be something the bowlers will take into consideration. Adds that the pitch looks good but there is a bit of moisture because of the pitch being under cover which will help the bowlers a bit which could see the captains choosing to bowl first.
UPDATE 12.50 pm GMT - The rain has subsided, and the covers are now being removed from the field. On-air reports also confirm that the toss will take place at the scheduled time.

Bangladesh, on the other hand, will be searching for a turnaround, hoping their seamers, who have been impressive, can lead the charge once more. Taskin Ahmed and Mustafizur Rahman have been commendable, but their spinners and top order need to step up if they are to challenge India's dominance in this series. The visitors have one last shot to restore some pride and give Mahmudullah a great farewell win - will they rise to the occasion, or will India complete a clean sweep? We shall find out soon as the toss is just around the corner. Stay tuned!

Welcome to the third and final T20I between India and Bangladesh at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium in Hyderabad! India have already clinched the series 2-0 and will be eager to finish the series on a high. Their dominant performance in the second T20I, where they posted their highest total against Bangladesh and secured a thumping 86-run win, showcased their T20 firepower. With Nitish Kumar Reddy, Rinku Singh, and the finishing prowess of Hardik Pandya and Riyan Parag, India’s batting looked unstoppable. The hosts might take this opportunity to test their bench strength in the final match.
... MATCH DAY ...
